title: Interleaved chunked tool callbacks: polyglot typed interop examples
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: deliver concrete, language-specific examples and interface additions for handling interleaved token chunks and out-of-band tool/function callbacks while preserving typed structured outputs across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs. This ticket captures a canonical pattern: chunk-framed streaming where model-generated text tokens, structured JSON emission, and tool invocation events can appear interleaved on the same stream; SDKs should expose ergonomic, type-safe primitives and a compat shim for older sync-only clients.

Background: Many clients want a single continuous response that mixes narrative text with structured events (e.g., JSON blocks) and tool invocation notifications (call + partial results). Existing SDKs support streaming text and simple tool call signals, but the practical patterns for: (1) framing partial JSON objects across chunks, (2) reconstituting typed events, and (3) providing a fallback synchronous API for legacy clients are inconsistent across languages. We need sample code, interface sketches, and tests for canonical behavior.

Non-goals: full refactor of existing runtime framing protocol; this ticket focuses on SDK surface + examples and a lightweight compatibility shim. Any server protocol changes will be coordinated in ENG-206000.
acceptance_criteria: TS SDK exposes a StreamReader that yields a typed union: {text_chunk, json_event, tool_call_event} and helpers to assemble partial JSON tokens into complete objects
Python SDK exposes an async iterator with similar typed events and a convenience 'replay_as_sync' shim that converts streaming events to synchronous blocking call for legacy code
Go SDK provides channel-based reader and a small helper library for incremental JSON decoding across chunk boundaries

Examples repo contains three end-to-end samples (ts/py/go) demonstrating: a) interleaved narrative + structured score JSON b) tool invocation start/partial/result events c) graceful fallback to sync-mode
Unit + integration tests that validate assembling split JSON across chunks, reordering resilience, and error handling for truncated events
Docs page in docs/sdk/interop describes the wire framing rules and idiomatic usage per language
Compatibility shim documented with migration steps and performance caveats
comments: 2026-02-16 Maya Chen: Kickoff - paired with runtime team to confirm we can surface a deterministic 'event_type' field on framed stream tokens. Runtime agreed to emit event_type: 'text'|'json_event'|'tool_event' on chunk envelopes for the next minor protocol rollout.

2026-02-18 Arjun Patel: Proposal - added TypeScript interface sketch to this ticket. See 'links' for PR draft. Key idea: StreamReader<T> where T = TextChunk | JsonEvent<TypedSchema> | ToolEvent. Provide 'assembleJson' utility that buffers consecutive json_event chunks and runs a streaming JSON decoder (incremental) to produce typed objects.

2026-02-20 Elena Ivanova (review): Request - ensure error semantics: decoder must surface a recoverable error for truncated JSON (allows caller to request re-fetch of missing data) and an unrecoverable error for mismatched schema. Also flagged KMS/security implications for tool_event payloads (may contain secrets).

2026-02-23 Arjun Patel: Implementation note - Python async iterator implemented with trio/asyncio compatibility shim. Added a 'replay_as_sync' helper that stitches events and blocks until the stream closes, returning a high-level Response object. Performance test shows ~3% latency increase for the shim; documented as expected.

2026-02-28 QA: Added tests for split-JSON (json_event fragments across five chunks). Found a bug where a JSON array start '[' in one chunk and remainder in another failed to parse. Fix: use incremental lexer that preserves structural state across chunk boundaries. Patch submitted in PR.
2026-03-03 Docs review (Lara O'Neill): requested clearer migration example from 'old_sync_invoke' to new streaming handler. Added code snippet and a table of compatibility tradeoffs.

2026-03-07 Security (Ravi Shah): reviewed tool_event handling. Recommendation: tool_event payloads must be redacted in telemetry by default; we added sdk flag 'emit_tool_payloads_in_telemetry=false' and documented in release notes.
2026-03-09 Arjun Patel: Submitted final PRs for TS/Go/py examples; CI green except for flaky windows go test. Added follow-up ENG-207999 to triage flaky CI. Preparing for merge pending doc signoff.
2026-03-10 Maya Chen: In Review - product review ok. Minor wording nits left in docs page. Schedule merge after doc edits and the CI fix in ENG-207999.
notes:
Design decisions: 1) prefer explicit event_type field rather than heuristic JSON detection to avoid false-positive structured output parsing; 2) SDKs will provide 'lenient' and 'strict' JSON assembly modes; 3) compatibility shim documented but not recommended for high-throughput production use.

Performance: measured end-to-end token throughput impact of streaming framing additions ~+1.5% p99 latency on small messages; batching configs can hide most of that overhead.

Migration path: publish examples, ship SDKs with opt-in flag 'enable_interleaved_streaming' enabled for beta users for 2 weeks, then enable by default after collected telemetry and docs.
